Planning a Material for each Borough.
A light weight, but sturdy material for Staaten
A Fae touched wood that almost mimics Iron's capability for Ferrytown
A shadowy glass that is nearly invisible to the eye for Kingsbridge.

Still need to come up w/ materials for Hampstead and The City

Staaten Steel- Weapons forged w/ this material are considered one weight less than normal weapons. Heavy weapons lose the Heavy Property, Non Light weapons gain the light property. Armor forged from this steel are lighter weight, removing any penalty to stealth checks and Heavy armors count as Medium armor and Medium armor count as Light armor.

Fae'd Oak- Weapons or Armor made from this wyld wood have no metal within them, but are just as sturdy as their metal counterparts. Armor made from this Fae'd Oak give resistance to Psychic and Force Damage. Weapons carved from Fae'd Oak are much less common, mainly because of their instability, when you Crit with these weapons roll on the Fae'd Oak wild magic table. (Need to make one)

Shadite Glass- While this material is malleable during crafting and as sharp as any steel blade, under certain circumstances it is more brittle than other materials. Due to it's glass like nature it is harder for foes to see coming and defend against, you gain +2 to hit with Shadite Glass Weapons. Unfortunately once tempered it becomes much more brittle, if you roll a natural 1 on an attack roll the blade shatters. (Can only make Bladed weapons with this)

Life Wires/Fibers- These threads are soaked in the leylines that meet in the City, absorbing the ambient magical energy. Robes weaved and leather armors stitched with these threads are able to once per day absorb one spell equal to or less than half your proficiency bonus. You may as an action, on your next turn, redirect the spell at another target per the spell’s rules. Bows and Crossbows strung with the thread count as a spell focus and deal additional force damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

This is great! These materials will pair nicely with the macro crafting system I'm cooking up. Instead of purchasing the material outright, what do you think about having it secured and rationed by each faction? To even get the opportunity to buy from them, you would have to get in good with their faction. Even then you may be limited to only buying enough for one crafting project at a time.

For The City, how about an energy based material? Weapons made with it gain the spell storing ability (say 1 spell level worth). Armor made with it will release the spell upon taking damage. Alternately, the energy material can harness the power of elements, and converts all weapon damage to magical elemental lightning damage.

Misty Shot
Firearm- Pistol (rare)
This Misty Shot pistol seems to always have a small amount of smoke streaming from its barrel. This magic firearm has a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls and deals 1d8 force damage instead of piercing damage. Twice per day you may use the Misty Shot to cast Misty Step, changing the range to match the pistols range.

The Tombstone
Shield 
A tombstone broken and taken from a graveyard, the name long worn away, and only the symbol of a god can just be seen. While wielding this shield you may use Turn Undead, per Cleric rules. Turn Undead used in this way does not scale, unless used by a Cleric.

Dr. Wynn’s Herbalist Bag
Wonderous item
A leather bag, made from different animal hides and stitched together with plant fibers, the interior has numerous pockets, each with an embroidered plant on the side. This bag counts as an herbalist’s kit and gives the wielder advantage on checks to find and identify herbs.
This bag also contains 10 charges, using the herbs you may spend up to three charges as a bonus action to heal someone 1d6 hit points per charge. The charges refresh if you spend at least an hour searching for herbs or spend at least 50gp on resupplying the bag.
<@!343605682580488215> I edited my material list w/ the City's material. Just think I need to do Hampstead and I'll have each of the Burroughs.

Shale Whip
Whip

The end of this finely crafted leather whip has several sharpened stones attached to it. You gain +1 to all attack and damage rolls with this weapon. You may use this whip to restrain a target. When you restrain them in this way you may deal an extra 1d4 piercing damage as the stones dig into them. Whenever they attempt to break the restrain they take another 1d4 piercing regardless if they are successful or not. As a bonus action you may pull on the whip to deal 1d4 piercing damage.

Belt of the Bastard Son
*wonderous item*

Runes representing each of the Giant clans are emblazoned on the front plate of this large weighted belt.

While wearing this belt your Strength becomes 20, if it isn't already higher. As a bonus action you can cast Enlarge on yourself once per long rest.

-Potential for effects of each giant clan?
XD

Grave Robber’s Crowbar

A rusty crowbar about 2.5 feet long with the initials R.C.G. carved into the side of it.
This crowbar acts as a club and a spellcasting focus. Once per day you can cast Animate Undead at 3rd level. The Grave Robber’s Crowbar has 3 charges and regains 1d3 charges daily at dawn. You can cast Inflict Wounds at 1st level by spending a charge.

Cleric’s compass
Requires attunement by a cleric.
A wristband with a compass mounted on it. The needle spins freely, pointing at the closest friendly target with the least amount of hit points. When you spend a spell slot to heal them they gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
 
Moon Thistle Bonsai
Requires attunement by a druid or ranger.
A small potted tree that's branches can be harvested daily to make 1d6 magical wooden ammunition for a Bow or Crossbow. It regrows every night as long as it bathes in moonlight.
You can trim up to 1d6 wooden magical ammo.

Bladed Shield
Shield
This shield has been modified to be more offensive, while retaining some of its defenses. While you have this shield equipped you only gain +1 to your AC. The edges have been sharpened and it’s been made light enough to swing it around like a blade. When you attack you deal 1d6 Slashing damage.
Twig of Power

Windswept Boots
Wonderous Item (requires attunement)

Light leather boots lined with Hippogriff down. Emblazoned in blue thread on the sides of the boots are lines resembling wind. While attuned to these boots you gain 5ft of movement speed as the wind seems to help push you along as you move. As a reaction to being targeted by a ranged attack you can force a quick wind to set the arrow or bolt of target, roll a d8 and subtract the number from the foe’s to hit roll. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest.

Stoppschild
greataxe 

A large metal octagon adorns the top of this odd choice for a weapon. This weapon gets +1 on attack and damage rolls and attack made with it count as magical. 

Once per day you can cast Command (halt) at 1st level as a bonus action. (DC 13)

Darling's Duster
Wonderous Item (requires attunement)

A maroon duster with mustard yellow silk lining covered in a paisley pattern of teal and aqua. The coat has four large pockets on the interior of the coat, each is large enough for a standard book. Stitched into one of the pockets is the word "Bookworm." As the coattails flow near the floor wisps of smoke or mist (your choice) pour from beneath.

While you are attuned to this item you can cast Fog Cloud at will, (1st level version, centered on yourself). Once per day you may also cast Gaseous Form on your self once per day, this ability recharges at dawn.
Book pockets! Yes!

Gauntlet of the Seasons
Wonderous Item (requires attunement)

This gauntlet appears to be carved from white oak. A pink Opal, red Jasper, orange Carnelian, and Lapis Lazuli are inlaid across the top of knuckles. Unarmed Strikes get +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls.
    These gauntlets have 5 charges, which are refreshed at dawn each morning. As a part of an attack action you may spend a charge to add the power of one of the seasons to your attack. The target takes an additional 2d4 damage. Choose one of the d4s. The number rolled on that die determines the additional damage type, as shown below.

D4| Damage Type
1    | Radiant
2   | Fire
3   | Necromantic
4   | Cold

If you roll the same number on both d4s, the power of the season leaps from the target to a different creature of your choice within 10 feet of it. Make an attack roll against the new target, and roll a new 2d4 damage roll, which could cause the power of the seasons to leap again.

A creature can be targeted only once by each use of the gauntlet.

McGinty’s Marvelous Elixir Demixer
Wondrous item

A ridiculous brass centrifuge with a place for two bottles to be placed. In the center of the centrifuge a crystal with a multicolored swirl in its center. Three buttons are on the face of the device, red, blue, green. This device can affect potions in several ways, depending on which button is selected.

Green- Mix effects of both liquids. I.e. a healing potion and a potion of invisibility mixed together will heal you for 2d4+2 and make you invisible.

Blue- Swap effects of liquids.

Red- Separates foreign material from a liquid. Only works when one bottle is empty. Removes poisons or other effects

Lectric Lasso
Whip, uncommon

This long flat cord of leather has a crackling arcane script along either side it’s length. You have +1 on attack rolls and damage. You can choose if the whip deals slashing or lightning damage. When you become attuned to this weapon you learn the Lightning Lure cantrip (Intelligence is your casting modifier). When you cast Lightning Lure using this weapon the range you can reach and the distance pulled are both doubled.

Sandilixer
Potion, uncommon

On the label of this deep crimson potion is a smiling and cartoonish fish person giving a thumbs up. Uncorked it smells strongly of sandiberries they are named after, when drunk it tastes just as strongly. You regain 3d4+3 hit points and gain enough nourishment to sustain a creature for the day.

War “Lock” Pick
Melee weapon (war pick), common 

The point on this War Pick has been smithed in a way that it can imitate a lock pick. This weapon doubles as thieves’ tools. When you make a check to unlock a door you may add your Strength modifier to the roll.

Wizard’s Beard and Hat
Rare, wondrous item (requires attunement by a spellcaster)

A fake wizard’s beard is attached to a pointy blue hat with silvery stars. When you attune to this item the beard attaches to your face and remains there until you unattune to the Beard and Hat. Once attuned you can change the appearance of the beard and hat, so long as you still appear to have a beard and hat on. You also gain +1 bonus to your Spell Attack, Spell Save, and AC while attuned to the Wizard’s Beard and Hat.

Crown of Cael'fii
Rare, Wondrous item (requires attunement by spellcaster)

A crown woven from twigs pulled from the branches of Cael'fii. Once attuned to the crown you can now cast the Shillelagh cantrip, if you don’t already know it. While attuned the cantrip is modified in the following ways:
-you may use this cantrip on any weapon made of wood.
-as an action, you may make a special attack that releases the magical powers imbued into the
weapon. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage (2d8) and the spell ends.

(courtesy of <@!237577351532249110> )
Coach Gun of Ash 
Rare Firearm (requires attunement)
This firearm is a short two barreled firearm with a single trigger weighing 5 lbs. It has a leather loop letting it hang off a belt while keeping it easily accessible. The barrels are always letting out small tendrils of smoke and soot. As an action you may draw this gun and fire. When you do, every creature in a 20 ft cone must make a Strength Save (DC 13) or take 4d4 fire damage and be knocked prone. After firing this, it takes 2 ammunition and 1 minute to reload. 

If an Arbiter is using this item, this item functions instead as the following: As an action or bonus action you may draw this gun and fire. When you do, every creature in a 20 ft cone must make a Strength Save (8 + your proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier) or take 4d4 force damage and be knocked 10 feet back and prone. If they make the saving throw, they take half the damage and are not knocked prone (but are still knocked back). Firing this also knocks the Arbiter using it 15 feet away from the cone, but they land on their feet. After firing this, it takes 2 ammunition and takes 2 rounds to reload.

Wilhelm’s Folly
Rare, quarterstaff (requires attunement)
Requires at least 16 Charisma

A staff designed for a mad comic who wished to “...really blow the audience away.” Atop the head of the staff is an enchanted metal cage that amplifies it’s users voice three fold. This staff has 7 charges. While attuned to it you may use the charges in the following ways.
    -Spend 3 charges to cast a 3rd level Pulse Wave spell (push only, save DC 15)
    -Spend 2 charges for the staff to act as a 3rd level Spiritual Weapon spell. When being used in this way you can’t use the staff for anything else until the spell ends.
    -Spend 3 charges to cast Hideous Laughter spell (save DC 15) on up to 3 targets within 30ft of each other.

This staff regains 1d6+1 charges daily at dawn.

rapier
